off.title: Sleep insights
off.body: Line up your watch's sleep with your food and workout log and see what may go with better or worse nights. Needs night data from the watch through JoyoFit.

settings.title: Free days
settings.body: Used to compare work-day and free-day sleep times. Change it if you work shifts.

consent.title: Sleep insights
consent.summary: When on, JoyoFit sends one summary per night to your account so JoyoRogo can line it up with your food and workout log.
consent.fields: Start and wake time, time asleep and awake, number of wake-ups, stage totals (if your watch has stages), the watch's sleep score, that night's HRV and resting heart rate, and nap times. If you set up a bedroom thermometer in JoyoFit: the average, lowest and highest room temperature and humidity during sleep.
consent.notSent: Not sent: per-minute heart rate or SpO2, location, food names to the AI model, and nights from before you turned this on.
consent.retention: Kept for 90 nights at most. Computed results are only a cache and are rebuilt.
consent.delete: Turning this switch off deletes all night data, the cache and hidden patterns at once. "Delete all data" removes them too.
consent.shared: Not shared with groups, the feed or AI connectors.
consent.disabledToast: Sleep insights off and night data deleted
consent.offConfirmBody: All stored night data will be deleted now.

caffeine.text: Your last coffee or caffeinated drink in the past 7 days was logged at {{time}}, about {{hours}} hours before you usually sleep. Caffeine takes about 5 hours on average to halve, but people differ (1.5 to 9.5 hours).
caffeine.sourceLabel: IOM: Caffeine for the Sustainment of Mental Task Performance

alcohol.text: Alcohol may make you fall asleep faster, but general research finds the second half of the night more disrupted and less REM. This is a general tip, not a result from your data.

regularity.text: Your bedtime moved by {{minutes}} minutes on average between nights this week. A consistent bedtime usually helps more than chasing duration.

jetlag.text: Your mid-sleep on free days is about {{minutes}} minutes {{direction}} than on work days. A shift this size is often called social jetlag.

room.text: Last night your room was about {{temp}} °C at {{rh}} % humidity. Humid heat tends to mean more waking and less deep sleep, but the comfortable range differs per person since bedding and clothing matter too.
room.sourceLabel: Okamoto-Mizuno 2012, Effects of thermal environment on sleep

caffeine.shorter: On {{exposed}} nights after coffee or a caffeinated drink within about 8 hours of bedtime, you slept {{minutes}} minutes shorter on average than on {{other}} nights without it.
caffeine.longer: On {{exposed}} nights after coffee or a caffeinated drink within about 8 hours of bedtime, you slept {{minutes}} minutes longer on average than on {{other}} nights without it.

dinner.more: On {{exposed}} nights with dinner less than 3 hours before bed, you were awake {{minutes}} minutes longer on average than on {{other}} other nights.
dinner.less: On {{exposed}} nights with dinner less than 3 hours before bed, you were awake {{minutes}} minutes less on average than on {{other}} other nights.

workout.more: On {{exposed}} nights after a vigorous workout of 20 minutes or more that ended within 3 hours of bedtime, you were awake {{minutes}} minutes longer on average than on {{other}} other nights.
workout.less: On {{exposed}} nights after a vigorous workout of 20 minutes or more that ended within 3 hours of bedtime, you were awake {{minutes}} minutes less on average than on {{other}} other nights.
workout.sourceLabel: Stutz 2019, Effects of evening exercise on sleep

regularity.shorter: On {{exposed}} nights when your bedtime moved more than 1 hour from your usual, you slept {{minutes}} minutes shorter on average than on {{other}} regular nights.
regularity.longer: On {{exposed}} nights when your bedtime moved more than 1 hour from your usual, you slept {{minutes}} minutes longer on average than on {{other}} regular nights.

tail.maybe: It may be related, but {{total}} nights are not enough to be sure.
tail.leaning: The pattern leans the same way across {{total}} nights, but it is still not proof of cause and effect.

temperature.more: On {{exposed}} nights with the room above {{value}} °C (your warmest third), you were awake {{minutes}} minutes longer on average than on {{other}} cooler nights.
temperature.less: On {{exposed}} nights with the room above {{value}} °C (your warmest third), you were awake {{minutes}} minutes less on average than on {{other}} cooler nights.
temperature.sourceLabel: Okamoto-Mizuno 2012, Effects of thermal environment on sleep

humidity.more: On {{exposed}} nights with room humidity above {{value}} % (your most humid third), you were awake {{minutes}} minutes longer on average than on {{other}} drier nights.
humidity.less: On {{exposed}} nights with room humidity above {{value}} % (your most humid third), you were awake {{minutes}} minutes less on average than on {{other}} drier nights.
humidity.sourceLabel: Okamoto-Mizuno 2012, Effects of thermal environment on sleep
